newsitem.title: USA: USF&G Q3 catastrophe losses totaled $45 mln.
newsitem.headline: USF&G Q3 catastrophe losses totaled $45 mln.

text.p: USF&G Corp said catastrophe losses totaled $45 million in the 1996 third quarter, $31 million of which was related to Hurricane Fran.

This level of quarterly losses was second only to the quarterly losses caused by Hurricane Andrew in 1992, and is significantly larger than the $4 million level for the same period last year, USF&G chairman Norman P. Blake Jr. said in a statement.
"Without the impact of excess catastrophe losses, our results would have been on target," Blake said.
After excluding catastrophe losses from both periods, the combined ratio improved 2.5 points, "a clear indicator of continuing improvement in underwriting performance," Blake said.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
USF&G said it experienced catastrophe losses in two unusual and unpredictable areas. The first was Hurricane Fran, which caused severe damage in a highly unlikely noncoastal inland area.
The second was a freak windstorm in Arizona that generated winds of 130 miles per hour, the highest ever recorded in the state. That storm produced $6.5 million in catastrophe losses, he said.

"Our fundamentals are strong. Although we are frustrated by the extent of the hurricane losses despite our significant reduction in exposures in catastrophe-prone areas based on our usage of sophisticated modeling techniques, we are not deterred by Mother Nature," Blake said.
But Blake said USF&G launched its new national Claim Reception Center in Tampa. which significantly enhances the service it can provide customers when they experience a loss.
The Center allowed its customers hit by Hurricane Fran to have direct access to its adjusters, who started the settlement process right over the phone.
Contractors were conferenced into the initial call so the clean up process could be initiated simultaneously.

"Our claim operation's goal is to be more than check handlers -- we want to be problem solvers. We believe our claim service can really be a competitive advantage for us when fully operational seven days a week, 24-hours a day beginning early next year," Blake said.
